For me, Inception is a puzzle, not cinema; a film that mistakes complexity for depth and substitutes its engineered calculations for cinematic experience. Nolan does not create dreams; he engineers them. Dream and the unconscious are reduced to a set of rules, layers, timings, instructions, and computational ticking clocks. Nolan is incapable, within the work, of allowing the real madness of dreams to take shape. Nolan does not set the unconscious and dreams free; Nolan writes a rulebook for the unconscious. The dream is not free; it has rules. The unconscious is not instinctive; it is calculable. Nolan wants to create the unconscious, but his unconscious is under control. As a result, because of Nolan’s misunderstanding of the uncontrollability of the unconscious and dreams, neither is actually created in the film. That is why the more the film talks about dreams, the less it creates dreams; the more it talks about the unconscious, the less it resembles the unconscious. As the film moves forward, more and more pieces are placed on the table: the first layer, the second layer, the third layer, time... and instead of dreaming, the viewer becomes a solver of a puzzle. As a result, watching the film is less like experiencing a world and more like solving a puzzle, and Christopher Nolan fails both at creating dreams and at creating the unconscious. Then action arrives in the film and devours everything: gunfire, chases, explosions, falling, an assault on the snowy fortress, and... as if even the unconscious in Nolan’s world cannot breathe without turning into an action sequence; a world that resembles a video game or a rule-bound action film more than a fluid and unpredictable unconscious. The visual effects are technically impressive; but being impressive, for me, is not form. The rotating hallway, the folded city, and the play with gravity, rather than becoming sensory experiences, are more like the film’s engineering calculations. It does not reach feeling and form, and does not turn into meaning. This chain does not take shape for me in Inception . Even the repeated close-ups of baby-faced DiCaprio’s face do not save anything for me. The camera repeatedly moves in close to Cobb’s face, but DiCaprio’s emotionless face remains incapable of saving the film. On the other hand, the film’s emotional center is also crushed beneath the weight of its engineered calculations. Cobb and Mal are supposed to be the heart of the film, but their grief and love often become fuel for that same mechanical narrative machine. In fact, feeling does not live within the image; rather, it has to move the puzzle forward. Feeling, instead of springing from within the image, is often a device for advancing the film’s mechanical puzzle. And this is where, for me, the film collapses. The film wants to engineer feeling. But feeling cannot be engineered. For me, cinema begins where the image can create feeling, build form, and arrive at meaning without relying on an instruction manual, but in this film, the puzzle becomes more important than the image, conceptualism moves ahead of feeling, and technique does not reach form. Ultimately, in Inception , I am faced with a work that explains dreams instead of dreaming; controls the unconscious instead of creating the unconscious; and architects the pieces of a puzzle with skill, without necessarily transforming these pieces into a living cinematic experience for the viewer. Nolan engineers the puzzle in Inception ; but in the process of engineering the puzzle, he loses cinema.

“I've put in so many enigmas and puzzles that it will keep the professors busy for centuries arguing over what I meant, and that is the only way of ensuring one's immortality.” - James Joyce I won't give this movie a particularly low rating because it's pretty entertaining as a Hollywood blockbuster. If you don't bring your brain with you, watching this is probably not much different from watching Spiderman. But if you unfortunately do bring your brain along, you'll start noticing the serious problems. If you treat it as soft sci-fi, then the psychological and philosophical depth is far too shallow to justify such an elaborate system. It's so unnecessarily complex that half the movie feels like sitting through a science lecture, with the characters constantly explaining the rules to you instead of actually being characters. If you treat it as hard sci-fi, it's even worse, because the system is filled with unexplainable loopholes and contradictions. I won't bother listing them here. You can easily google them. All this complexity actually made a fairly straightforward blockbuster less enjoyable for me. It feels like a movie desperately trying to convince you how clever it is, when underneath all the puzzles, there's surprisingly little to chew on.

É extremamente elaborado, mas quase nunca parece fértil. Estamos literalmente entrando na cabeça dos personagens, mas é difícil ter alguma simpatia por eles. Os sonhos não revelam nada profundamente particular, e todos parecem existir dentro da mesma estética fria e genérica de blockbuster. O inconsciente acaba parecendo um ambiente corporativo. E os personagens também não ajudam. Achei difícil me importar com quase qualquer um deles, e o drama do protagonista e da mulher me pareceu muito mais funcional para a trama do que realmente emocionante. A única parte que me tocou foi a do DiCaprio precisar aceitar que não pode continuar vivendo preso à imagem da mulher que perdeu, porque, de alguma maneira, isso é identificável para todo mundo. A ideia de esquecer alguém, ou, pelo menos, aceitar que a memória dessa pessoa não pode continuar controlando sua vida é genuinamente bonita. É uma pena que o filme precise de tanta maquinaria em volta para chegar a algo tão singelo. A primeira metade foi insuportável. Muito chata e sem graça, parecendo só um filme de espião com uma ideia mais interessante. A segunda metade melhora bastante, porque finalmente existe alguma tensão e a estrutura dos sonhos começa a produzir consequências de verdade, mas ainda fiquei com a sensação de estar vendo um conceito extraordinário sendo utilizado de maneira infrutífera. O final, porém, é instigante, porque finalmente existe alguma ambiguidade de verdade. Se ele está sonhando, é nota 8. Se não está, é nota 4. Como não sei, fica no meio-termo: 6/10. Porque nos sonhos, estamos juntos.

I remember it being exciting, new and so much fun on first viewing, so awe inspiring in theatres.  The movie falter a bit on repeat viewing, (there’s an emptiness that peaks its head out every once in a while), but it does hold up. The team assembles, they all get their moments to shine, and they scatter with a knowing nod at the end of the robbery. This film has a LOT of things going on, it really walks a tightrope without managing to fall onto the hard pavement, although there are some close calls.  As is normal with a Nolan film, it’s too long. I think some of that could have been dealt with in the editing, but I’m not entirely sure what I would cut. It’s not really a detriment to the film, but why does Nolan insist on weird names like Ariatne? I slept on Inception, no pun intended, for quite a while before finally checking it out.  I was aware of the metaphor for filmmaking and such and some complaints that for a world set in dreams, it's rather unambitious in dealing with the unreal.  And while I'm sure more could have been done to make something more challenging and experimental, the film as is acts as a fantastic ride while being a metaphor for being Christopher Nolan, a man whose work probably keeps him from his kids. But I think part of the reason I forgive the lack of being overtly fantastical in the way that a Nightmare on Elm Street might be is that because it is about filmmaking, it is a fun heist movie exploring the idea of using the pieces and ideas a viewer already knows and how when properly utilized can be a way to bring in a new idea to the viewer.  If anything, I feel this is not what Nolan thinks he does specifically but also aspirational, in hopes of being the man who can put in a new idea.  And like a thief it needs to be done with tact so eventually the "target" and become a part of the same side, with your defenses overcome in the face of an idea baked in emotion. But if this was all "idea" it wouldn't work.  The way it works is that Nolan is a tactful and even fun filmmaker, even if the films aren't big on laughs.  It's easy to think of Nolan as a maker of blockbusters that feel more "dour" but he is actually an expert ride-crafter where the goal is to make a blockbuster that still wants to explore ideas but are also a blast to watch.

Rewatched Inception to put my thoughts in which film I thought was better- Paprika or this. Getting the record straight: Inception, despite being an exposition-heavy/slow paced film, is better overall in comparison to Paprika. My opinion why is this: First off, Inception has that sort of style in which everything is difficult, yet fairly easy to understand. It may be slow, but there are multiple visually pleasing scenes/intense action sequences that keep the audience in put, also with more actually innovative narrative that just begged to be seen. Second, paprika? One can’t deny the possible influence it had on Inception, but you also can’t deny the fact that Paprika relied more heavily on a style-over-substance approach and “dream logic” to patch up its obviously weak narrative. Many that love Paprika usually trash Inception without ever knowing that Inception at least has something to hold bound to instead of what’s basically a art-showcase. There’s too much going on to even care, especially when Paprika is already slow as hell. In a simple summary, Inception may have copied Paprika- we’ll never know, but it surely became superior to it and told a much more engrossing story than Paprika will ever be. 8/10.

Desde el principio presenta una idea muy original: entrar en los sueños de otras personas para obtener o implantar información (como es el caso en esta película). Es un concepto complejo, pero la película logra desarrollarlo de una forma que se vuelve cada vez más interesante conforme avanza la historia. Lo que más me gustó fue precisamente el concepto de los sueños, las actuaciones y los giros de trama. La forma en que Nolan construye distintos niveles de sueños y hace que todos funcionen al mismo tiempo es algo que pocas películas han intentado hacer. Leonardo DiCaprio hace una gran actuación como Cobb. Además de liderar al equipo, consigue transmitir el peso emocional que carga durante toda la historia. También me gustó mucho la dinámica que tiene con los demás miembros del grupo, ya que hace que la misión se sienta más real y que te intereses por lo que les ocurre a todos. Mi escena favorita fue la batalla final. Es un momento lleno de tensión, acción y emoción donde todas las piezas de la historia comienzan a encajar. Además, la forma en que se conectan los diferentes niveles de sueños hace que la secuencia sea aún más emocionante. La música es otro de los puntos fuertes de la película. Ayuda a crear una sensación constante de misterio, urgencia y grandeza que encaja perfectamente con la historia. Algo que también me parece destacable es el uso de efectos prácticos. Nolan evitó depender completamente del CGI y utilizó escenarios reales, efectos físicos y cámaras IMAX para muchas secuencias importantes. Esto hace que escenas como los pasillos giratorios o los cambios de gravedad se sigan viendo espectaculares incluso años después de su estreno. Una película inteligente, emocionante y visualmente espectacular que demuestra por qué Christopher Nolan es uno de los directores más importantes.

Настоящим тотемом Кобба был не волчок (он принадлежал Мэл), а его кольцо. Во всех снах он носит кольцо на руке, а во всех сценах в реальности — нет. В финальной сцене кольца на его пальце нет. Дети: В воспоминаниях и снах Кобб никогда не видит лиц своих детей, и они всегда одеты одинаково. В финале они наконец оборачиваются, а в титрах указаны другие актеры, так как дети подросли. Сам Кристофер Нолан на Variety отмечал, что интеллектуально Кобб находится в реальности, но эмоционально ему уже всё равно. Он уходит к детям, даже не дожидаясь, упадет ли волчок. Мне было проще понять идею совместных снов, если посмотреть аниме которым вдохновлялся Нолан:"Паприка". Резюмируя, фильм оставил очень странное неописуемое чувство после просмотра.
